name: SigMF Raw-IQ Capture Source Nodes
description: Public raw-IQ archives -> SDS $IQC pointer records (typed contracts 1.0: FlatBuffers only, no JSON and no base64 between modules). Two pure flow nodes: `request` turns a TimerTick into ONE bulk HttpRequest (HREQ) GET of the configured archive's metadata index (default IQEngine: https://www.iqengine.org/api/datasources/local/local/meta, anonymous, no token, ~31 MB, 36,636 SigMF documents) whose CONTEXT is the parse job, one size-prefixed IngestRequest (INGQ) skeleton (schema IQC.fbs, provider, the adapter's source name, source URL, reconcile None, archive naming), echoed by hostcap/http-request in the HttpResponse; `parse` reads that HttpResponse (HRSP), resolves the source adapter from the job's source name through the registry, reads the archive coordinates (iqengine_base_url / iqengine_account / iqengine_container) from the same node CONFIG request used, decodes each SigMF document and emits a size-prefixed $IQC record stream, the IngestRequest for hostcap/storage-ingest (the job completed with the batch id and provenance) and the HttpResponse verbatim as the raw document. $IQC IS A POINTER RECORD: it carries where the samples are (PAYLOADS[].URL), what they hash to (BYTE_SHA512 from SigMF core:sha512) and nothing else — CUSTODY stays UPSTREAM_ONLY and no payload is ever mirrored. SigMF publishes HERTZ, so SAMPLE_RATE_HZ / CENTER_FREQ_HZ / FREQ_*_EDGE_HZ carry the value unconverted ($RFB's MHz convention is deliberately NOT adopted) and DATATYPE is the SigMF token verbatim. GEOLOCATION is omitted entirely when the source published no position, and a transposed lat/lon is refused rather than swapped. LICENCE IS PER RECORDING: core:license rides verbatim and an absent one means UNKNOWN TERMS, never public domain; the batch source tags name no licence. The source-adapter registry ships exactly one adapter, the one whose anonymous read surface was verified live; a stub adapter that fabricates data is forbidden and an unknown adapter id (request) or source name (parse) fails closed. Node CONFIG through the builtin plugin.getConfig hostcall (SDS $PIV, one ModuleConfig FlatBuffer): sigmf_adapter, sigmf_source_url, iqengine_base_url, iqengine_account, iqengine_container, sigmf_http_timeout_ms, sigmf_provider_id, sigmf_if_none_match, sigmf_if_modified_since, sigmf_record_cap (integers as a number or a decimal string; anything else refused). No capabilities: this node performs no I/O — http and storage are the generic hostcap connector nodes. HTTP 304 Not Modified is accepted, never treated as a failed fetch: the parse method emits a single FlowNotice (Unchanged, not-modified) on its 'unchanged' port and nothing else, so no batch is stored or announced.

sequentialJustification.detail: Both methods are pure single-pass transforms over one fetched JSON document: `request` builds one HttpRequest from node CONFIG, and `parse` walks the archive's capture documents once, emitting one $IQC record per document into a single append-only stream. There is no shared mutable state, no worker pool, no fan-out and nothing for a second thread to do; the whole cost is one linear scan of the metadata index. This guest can never spawn a thread, so it compiles wasi-sequential rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

methods.description: Builds the archive bulk-metadata fetch from a TimerTick: ONE bulk HttpRequest per cycle — the per-file metadata route exists but walking it would be a 36,636-request crawl of a community-run service — with an identifying User-Agent, conditional-request validators from node CONFIG when set, and the parse job in CONTEXT (one size-prefixed IngestRequest naming the adapter's source name). An adapter id (sigmf_adapter) absent from the registry fails closed. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is now ENFORCED IN CODE, not merely declared. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime - space_data_module_runtime_begin_node_invocation pops the node whole queue port-blind up to the drain budget (64) - so a node that read ordinal 0 of a port and returned used to destroy every other frame it was handed there, with nothing re-delivering them and nothing logging the loss (live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider). A surplus is now refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count. See graph task modules-guest-nodes-drop-batched-frames.

acceptedTypeSets.description: TimerTick (module-sdk runtime type TICK) from the flow's timer trigger.

inputPorts.description: Cron timer tick (its fields are not read).

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpRequest (HREQ) for hostcap/http-request: GET the archive's bulk metadata index, headers user-agent / accept (and if-none-match / if-modified-since from CONFIG), TIMEOUT_MS sigmf_http_timeout_ms; CONTEXT: the parse job, one size-prefixed IngestRequest (SCHEMA IQC.fbs, TAGS PROVIDER_ID / SOURCE_NAME the adapter's source name (IQEngine) / SOURCE_URL, RECONCILE None, ARCHIVE sigmf / <adapter>-meta.json).

methods.description: Reads the HttpResponse carrying the archive metadata index and its job (CONTEXT), resolves the source adapter from the job's TAGS.SOURCE_NAME (unknown fails closed) and decodes each SigMF document into an $IQC pointer record (Hz unconverted, DATATYPE verbatim, SEGMENTS/ANNOTATIONS/EXTENSIONS carried, GEOLOCATION omitted when unpublished or out of WGS-84 range, licence per recording, PAYLOADS pointing upstream with CUSTODY UPSTREAM_ONLY), emitting the $IQC stream, the IngestRequest for storage-ingest and the HttpResponse verbatim for archiving. The archive coordinates come from node CONFIG (iqengine_base_url / iqengine_account / iqengine_container, the defaults request uses); the record cap from sigmf_record_cap. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is now ENFORCED IN CODE, not merely declared. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime - space_data_module_runtime_begin_node_invocation pops the node whole queue port-blind up to the drain budget (64) - so a node that read ordinal 0 of a port and returned used to destroy every other frame it was handed there, with nothing re-delivering them and nothing logging the loss (live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider). A surplus is now refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count. See graph task modules-guest-nodes-drop-batched-frames. HTTP 304 Not Modified is accepted: the host presents the ETag / Last-Modified it recorded from the last 2xx for this URL, so an unchanged document answers 304 with no body. The method then emits a single FlowNotice on its 'unchanged' port and nothing else, so no batch is stored or announced. Any other non-200 status (or a failed exchange, STATUS 0) fails closed with nothing emitted.

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpResponse (HRSP) from hostcap/http-request: STATUS, HEADERS, BODY verbatim, the request's CONTEXT (the job, a size-prefixed IngestRequest), RETRIEVED_MS.

inputPorts.description: The HTTP response carrying the archive metadata index, its job echoed in CONTEXT.

acceptedTypeSets.description: IngestRequest (INGQ) for hostcap/storage-ingest: SCHEMA IQC.fbs, TAGS (PROVIDER_ID, SOURCE_NAME, BATCH_ID = sha256 of the payload, SOURCE_URL, CONTENT_KEY_ID public, SOURCE_PEER source:sigmf; no batch LICENSE: licence is per recording), RECONCILE from the job (None), ARCHIVE from the job, PROVENANCE (status, validators, retrieval time, parser, source / normalized SHA-256, counts, WARNINGS naming the capture documents the record cap left unread, the documents skipped for no archive identity and the geolocations refused out of range).
The HttpResponse (HRSP) the batch was made from, verbatim: its BODY is the archive's metadata index storage-ingest archives under the request's ARCHIVE naming.
FlowNotice (FNTC): KIND Unchanged, SCHEMA IQC.fbs, PROVIDER_ID, SOURCE_NAME, REASON not-modified, ITEMS the source URL, AT_MS the host's retrieval time.

outputPorts.description: Emitted ONLY when the fetch answered HTTP 304 Not Modified (the host sent the recorded ETag / Last-Modified validators): one notice frame and no meta/records/raw frames, so the ingest node never becomes ready and nothing is stored or announced.
